newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat ahead of new supply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- flat ahead of new supply.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were flat in early Tuesday trading as market participants said they were waiting for direction from several large new issue pricings.
"We're just kind of sitting here waiting to see how things are priced," one trader said. "I think the deals will probably go pretty well."
Among the day's largest issues are a $300 million Florida Department of Environmental Protection deal, set for competitive bids at 1100 EDT.
In negotiated action, Smith Barney Inc. tentatively priced $150 million King County, Wash., general obligation bonds at a top yield of 5.80 percent in 2011.

J.P. Morgan Securities on Tuesday began a one-day retail order period for a $528 million New York City Municipal Assistance Corporation deal. The firm offered the 2005 maturity at a 5.25 percent yield.
The preliminary pricing is expected Wednesday.
Also Wednesday, Goldman Sachs & Co. is expected to price a $500 million Chicago School Reform Board of Trustees offering.
Supply is also a factor in the government securities market. The Treasury is set to auction $17 billion of two-year notes Tuesday, and $12.5 billion of five-year notes on Wednesday.
Ahead of the auctions, the government long bond was off 2/32 at 94-6/32 to yield 7.10 percent.
In the muni secondary, bids on Denver Airport MBIA 5.6s of 2020 were up two basis points to 5.95 percent. Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2025 were up one basis point to 5.87 percent.

In debt futures, the June municipal contract was up 3/32 at 112-22/32, while June T-bonds were unchanged at 107-21/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts was 161 ticks, widening three ticks from Monday's close.
